pr_title: [Python] Improve performance of conversion to Numpy/Pandas for nested lists
pr_body:
This PR fixes #8623

Previously we were creating python `list` objects, now we create `numpy.array` objects instead.
This has the advantage that we no longer use the slow tuple-at-a-time conversion we used previously, and also in most cases the memory usage for converting nested lists goes down significantly because we make fewer small allocations.
pr_comments:
Thanks for the PR! Looks great - I played around with this a bit and ran some benchmarks out of curiosity, here are some timings:

|                   Benchmark                    | v0.10.0 | New  |
|------------------------------------------------|---------|------|
| 1M Boolean Lists (1K rows each)                | 82.8s   | 6.7s |
| 1M Integer Lists (1K rows each)                | 101.1s  | 4.9s |
| 100K string lists (1K rows each)               | 21.1s   | 7.6s |
| 100K nested integer lists (10 * 100 rows each) | 16.7s   | 8.1s |


###### Boolean List

```sql
select [x%2==0 for x in generate_series(i, i + 1000, 1)] l from range(1000000) t(i);
```

###### Integer List

```sql
select generate_series(i, i + 1000, 1) l from range(1000000) t(i);
```

###### String List

```sql
select [concat('thisisastring', x) for x in generate_series(i, i + 1000, 1)] l from range(100000) t(i);
```

###### Nested List

```sql
select [
	generate_series(i, i + 100, 1),
	generate_series(i + 100, i + 200, 1),
	generate_series(i + 200, i + 300, 1),
	generate_series(i + 300, i + 400, 1),
	generate_series(i + 400, i + 500, 1),
	generate_series(i + 500, i + 600, 1),
	generate_series(i + 600, i + 700, 1),
	generate_series(i + 700, i + 800, 1),
	generate_series(i + 800, i + 900, 1),
	generate_series(i + 900, i + 1000, 1)
] l from range(100000) t(i);
```

issue_context.title: High memory usage when reading boolean list column from parquet
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

Memory usage explodes when I try to materialize a 100k row BOOL[] column(ie each row value is [ False, True....1000 elements]) as a pandas dataframe from parquet files. 
At same time, if I try to materialize the column as a arrow table first and then convert it to a pandas dataframe, memory usage doesn't spike.


### To Reproduce

```
 parquet_path = '<path>'

 query = "select \"boolean_list_column\" from read_parquet('{}/*.parquet')".format(parquet_path)
#memory usage explodes to like 30GB
 column = duckdb.sql(query).df()

#memory usage stays level around 2GB
 column = duckdb.sql(query).arrow().to_pandas()
```

### OS:

mac

### DuckDB Version:

0.8.1

### DuckDB Client:

python

### Full Name:

Paul Cherian

### Affiliation:

qualtrics

### Have you tried this on the latest `master` branch?

I have tested with a master build

### Have you tried the steps to reproduce? Do they include all relevant data and configuration? Does the issue you report still appear there?

- [X] Yes, I have
comments: Hi @PaulCherian, thanks for reporting this. Could you please provide a script that generates a Parquet file that reproduces this issue?

You can use the snippet below to generate the parquet files
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

parquet_file_path = '/tmp/test.parquet'

rows = 1000000
width = 1000
column = np.random.choice([False, True], size=(rows, width))
df = pd.DataFrame({'bool_list_column': np.zeros(rows, dtype=object)})
for i in range(rows):
    df.iloc[i, 0] = column[i]
df.to_parquet(parquet_file_path)
```

Here is the memory usage graph I generated using `memray` when running
```python
import duckdb
import time

parquet_file_path = '/tmp/test.parquet'

print('reading parquet using duckdb')
start = time.time()
query = "select bool_list_column from read_parquet('{}')".format(
    parquet_file_path)
checkbox = duckdb.sql(query).df()
print('took {} seconds'.format(time.time() - start))
```
The whole process took ~200s to run
![newplot (16)](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/assets/13074900/f5efe72f-61d2-4344-a806-313bf259ae45)

Here is the memory usage graph I generated using memray when running
```
print('reading parquet using duckdb')
start = time.time()
query = "select bool_list_column from read_parquet('{}')".format(
    parquet_file_path)
checkbox = duckdb.sql(query).arrow().to_pandas()
print('took {} seconds'.format(time.time() - start))
```
The whole process took only ~20s(significantly faster than .df())
